nodes.title: Calibration score

nodes.summary: For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a grid $\{0, 1/k, \dots, 1\}$ and a randomised forecasting rule such that, against every Nature who chooses each outcome knowing the past but not the current randomisation, the calibration score after $t$ rounds is below $\varepsilon$ with probability greater than $1 - \varepsilon$ for all large $t$. Deterministic forecasters cannot achieve this (Oakes 1985; Dawid 1985).
nodes.title: Asymptotic calibration

nodes.summary: In Jordan's family of three-player two-action games with parameters $a_1, a_2, a_3$ close to $1$, where each player wants to mismatch the next, the unique Nash equilibrium has player $i$ play its first action with probability $a_{i-1}/(a_{i-1} + 1)$ (indices mod 3).
nodes.title: Nash equilibrium of Jordan's games

nodes.title: Uncoupled dynamics do not lead to Nash equilibrium

nodes.summary: Let $|c_i| \le M$ and $\mu > 2M(|S_i| - 1)$ for every player $i$. If the first round is arbitrary and, given the history, the players choose the next round's actions independently, each according to regret matching, then almost surely the empirical distributions of play converge to the set of correlated equilibria. Convergence is to the set, not to a point.
nodes.title: Regret matching leads to correlated equilibria
